title: Run the Three-Way Match
subtitle: Reconcile the invoice, the PO, and the receipt
scenario: It is 11:15 AM. Three trusted records are lined up: the Invoice ($1,220 for 500 bolts), the PO ($1,200 for 500 ordered), and the Receipt (500 received). Now do the reconciliation the whole desk turns on - compute the price variance, compare it to the tolerance band, confirm the quantities, and declare the result.
input: Invoice total: 1220.00. PO total: 1200.00. Ordered: 500. Received: 500. Tolerance Policy v1.0.0: price variance allowed within the LARGER of 2% of the PO (2% of 1200.00 = 24.00) or 25.00; quantity must match exactly.
instructions: Compute the price variance: invoice total minus PO total.
Compute the variance percent: variance over PO total, times 100, rounded to 2 decimals.
Compute the tolerance band: the larger of 2% of the PO (24.00) and 25.00.
Set qtyMatch (received equals ordered) and withinTolerance (variance within the band).
Declare matchResult, and return one valid JSON object. Use numbers for the amounts.
copilotPrompt: Compute a three-way match JSON record: invoiceTotal, poTotal, variance (invoice minus PO), variancePct (variance / PO * 100, 2 decimals), toleranceBand (larger of 2% of PO or 25), qtyMatch, withinTolerance, and matchResult. Use numbers.
successMessage: Three-way match complete. Variance 20.00 is within the 25.00 band - a clean, matched line.
editorHelper: Reconcile the three records and declare the result.

intro.heading: Before you pay: reconcile all three

sections.title: Three records must agree
sections.body: Order, delivery, and bill each come from a different owner. The three-way match is where they finally meet: only when all three line up does the desk agree to pay.

sections.title: Price variance is arithmetic
sections.body: Invoice 1220.00 minus PO 1200.00 is a 20.00 variance, or 1.67% of the PO. These are computed, not judged - which is exactly why they can be automated.

sections.title: Compare to the written band
sections.body: The Tolerance Policy allows the larger of 2% of the PO (24.00) or 25.00, so the band is 25.00. Under larger-of, that single band is the whole test: a 20.00 variance sits inside 25.00, so the price leg passes.

sections.title: Quantity is exact
sections.body: Received 500 equals ordered 500, so qtyMatch is true with no tolerance. Price within band plus an exact quantity match makes this a clean, matched line.

fieldGuide.meaning: The amount the invoice asks for.
fieldGuide.hint: From the Invoice Record - store the number only.

fieldGuide.meaning: The amount the PO agreed to.
fieldGuide.hint: From the PO Register - store the number only.
1220 minus 1200. A positive number means the invoice is higher.

fieldGuide.meaning: The variance as a percent of the PO total, to 2 decimals.
The larger of 2% of the PO and the absolute floor.
fieldGuide.hint: 2% of 1200 is 24; the floor is 25; the larger is 25.

fieldGuide.meaning: Whether the price variance is inside the tolerance band.
fieldGuide.hint: 20 is within the 25.00 band, so true.

fieldGuide.meaning: The overall outcome of the match.
fieldGuide.hint: Price within tolerance and an exact quantity match makes this matched.

takeaway.heading: Three-way match complete
points: You reconciled three independently owned records - invoice, PO, and receipt - into one result.
The price variance (20.00) and percent (1.67) are computed from the totals, not judged by eye.
The tolerance band is the larger of 2% of the PO (24.00) and 25.00, so 25.00 - and the 20.00 variance sits inside it.
Quantity matches exactly and price is within tolerance, so the line is matched.
The workflow can now decide, on numbers alone, whether an invoice line is clean or an exception.
